ei.title: Chapter 5-14 2번: Finding Pluto Through Visual Movement
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: The ability to detect visual movement played an interesting role in the history of astronomy. In 1930, Clyde Tombaugh was searching the skies for a possible undiscovered planet beyond Neptune. He photographed each region of the sky twice, several days apart. Stars essentially remain unmoving in photos, while a planet moves from one photo to the next. However, how would he find a small dot that moved among all the countless unmoving dots in the sky? He put each pair of photos on a machine that would flip back and forth between one photo and the other. When he came to one pair of photos, he immediately noticed one dot moving as the machine flipped back and forth. He identified that dot as Pluto, which astronomers now list as a dwarf planet.

questions.passage: The ability to (A)[overlook / detect] visual movement played an interesting role in the history of astronomy. In 1930, Clyde Tombaugh was searching the skies for a possible undiscovered planet beyond Neptune. He photographed each region of the sky twice, several days apart. Stars essentially remain unmoving in photos, while a planet moves from one photo to the next. However, how would he find a small dot that moved among all the (B)[countless / few] unmoving dots in the sky? He put each pair of photos on a machine that would flip back and forth between one photo and the other. When he came to one pair of photos, he (C)[immediately / eventually] noticed one dot moving as the machine flipped back and forth. He identified that dot as Pluto, which astronomers now list as a dwarf planet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 시각적 움직임을 감지하는(detect) 능력, 수많은(countless) 점들, 즉시(immediately) 알아챘다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① overlook — countless — immediately (A 반대: 감지하다→간과하다)
✅ ② detect — countless — immediately — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ detect — few — immediately (B 반대: 수많은→거의 없는)
❌ ④ detect — countless — eventually (C 반대: 즉시→결국)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 아직 발견되지 않은(undiscovered) 행성, 별은 그대로 있고(remain), 그 점을 명왕성으로 확인했다(identified).

❌ ② familiar — remain — identified (A 반대: 발견되지 않은→익숙한)
❌ ③ undiscovered — leave — identified (B 반대: 그대로 있다→떠나다)
❌ ④ undiscovered — remain — overlooked (C 반대: 확인하다→간과하다)
det.tip: undiscovered(발견되지 않은) ↔ familiar(익숙한), remain(그대로 있다) ↔ leave(떠나다)

② moving — 원문은 unmoving(움직이지 않는) ←정답
③ pair — 한 쌍, 원문 일치
④ identified — 확인하다, 원문 일치

❌ ④ remained — 그대로 있다 (움직임을 포착한 맥락과 반대)
det.tip: noticed one dot moving = 한 점이 움직이는 것을 알아챘다

questions.passage: The ability to detect visual movement played an interesting role in the history of astronomy. In 1930, Clyde Tombaugh was searching the skies for a possible undiscovered planet beyond Neptune. He photographed each region of the sky twice, several days apart. Stars essentially remain unmoving in photos, while a planet moves from one photo to the next. However, how would he find a small dot that moved among all the countless unmoving dots in the sky? He put each pair of photos on a machine that would __________ between one photo and the other. When he came to one pair of photos, he immediately noticed one dot moving as the machine flipped back and forth. He identified that dot as Pluto, which astronomers now list as a dwarf planet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그는 사진을 한 장과 다른 한 장 '사이를 휙휙 번갈아 넘기는'(flip back and forth) 기계에 올려놓았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① flip back and forth — 앞뒤로 휙휙 넘기다 (between one photo and the other와 연결) ←정답
❌ ② remain completely still — 완전히 가만히 있다 (기계가 사진을 번갈아 보여줘야 함, 반대)
❌ ③ move several days apart — 며칠 간격으로 움직이다 (사진 촬영 간격을 오용)
❌ ④ search the whole sky — 하늘 전체를 뒤지다 (기계의 동작이 아님)
det.tip: flip back and forth = 두 사진을 앞뒤로 번갈아 넘기다 (움직이는 점을 눈에 띄게 함)
